# Maven Build Lifecycle — Legacy CI Repair Workflow

## Core rule: reproduce the target CI before changing the project

For build-repair tasks, the first successful local command is not enough. The
failure must be reproduced under the toolchain and Maven command used by the
target CI. Read the repository's CI configuration (`.travis.yml`, workflow
files, wrapper scripts, build POMs) before interpreting any compiler or
dependency error.

Record at least:

```bash
java -version
javac -version
mvn -version
```

If the repository declares a historical JDK and the container's default Java
is newer, switch to the declared JDK *before* patching project files. A failure
caused only by running an old project on a modern JDK is not evidence that the
project should be migrated.

can be reproduced with:

```bash
source /opt/jdk_switcher/jdk_switcher.sh
jdk_switcher use openjdk7
export TRAVIS_JDK_VERSION=openjdk7
java -version
```

```bash
mvn -Dhttps.protocols=TLSv1.2 -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify \
  --fail-at-end -Dsource.skip=true -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true
```

# Maven Dependency Management

Master Maven dependency management including dependency declaration, scope management, version resolution, BOMs, and dependency tree optimization.

## Overview

Maven's dependency management is a cornerstone of Java project build systems. It handles transitive dependencies, version conflicts, and provides mechanisms for controlling dependency resolution across multi-module projects.

## Dependency Declaration

### Basic Dependency

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
    <version>3.2.0</version>
</dependency>
```

### Dependency with Scope

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
    <version>5.10.1</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

### Optional Dependencies

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.google.code.findbugs</groupId>
    <artifactId>jsr305</artifactId>
    <version>3.0.2</version>
    <optional>true</optional>
</dependency>
```

## Dependency Scopes

### Available Scopes

| Scope | Compile CP | Test CP | Runtime CP | Transitive |
|-------|-----------|---------|------------|------------|
| compile | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| provided | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| runtime | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| test | No | Yes | No | No |
| system | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| import | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |

diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The location-only hint points to incorrect or underspecified guidance in maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md about how to diagnose dependency-resolution failures inside nested Maven test projects (e.g., Maven Invoker/IT projects under src/it or similar) and what scope of modifications is acceptable. This can mislead the repair workflow into changing the wrong POM (root vs nested test project) or applying dependency fixes too broadly (e.g., global exclusions) instead of targeting the nested integration-test project’s own POM/settings, causing persistent build failures or unintended breakage.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Section(s) covering reproduction/repair of legacy CI builds and Maven Invoker integration tests likely lack precise instructions for resolving dependencies in nested test projects (integration-test fixtures) and for constraining edits to the correct POM(s). The skill may currently imply resolving dependencies only at the top-level reactor or may encourage global dependency modifications, which is often wrong for nested invoker projects that have independent POMs, repositories, mirrors, and parent resolution rules.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Revise/add a dedicated subsection in maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md explaining: (1) how to detect nested Maven test projects (e.g., src/it/** with pom.xml, invoker plugin usage, maven-invoker-plugin, maven-verifier), (2) how to reproduce dependency resolution inside those nested projects (run mvn in the nested directory or via invoker with -X, check effective-pom, dependency:tree, dependency:get with same settings.xml/mirrors), (3) clarify parent/artifact resolution rules for nested projects (relativePath, local repo reuse, need to install parent artifacts first), and (4) strictly define modification scope: prefer fixing the nested project’s own pom.xml or the invoker configuration; only change root dependencyManagement/plugins if the dependency is shared and proven to be the actual source; avoid blanket exclusions/versions that affect unrelated modules. Include explicit “do/don’t” examples and a checklist for deciding where to patch.
